title: Nathan's Parable of the Ewe Lamb
text:
King David had taken Bathsheba, the wife of his soldier Uriah, and when she became pregnant he arranged for Uriah to be killed in battle. Then he married her. No one dared to confront the king.

The prophet Nathan came to David with what sounded like a legal case. There were two men in a city, he said, one rich and one poor. The rich man had a great many flocks and herds. The poor man had nothing but one little ewe lamb that he had bought and raised. It grew up with his children, ate from his plate, drank from his cup and slept in his arms. It was like a daughter to him. When a traveler came to visit the rich man, he did not want to take an animal from his own flocks, so he took the poor man's lamb and cooked it for his guest.

David burned with anger. He swore that the man who had done this deserved to die, and that he must repay the lamb four times over, because he had done it without pity.

Nathan said to David: "You are the man." He went on to name what David had done to Uriah. David answered: "I have sinned against the Lord."
lesson: It is easy to see injustice in others and hard to see it in yourself, especially when no one can challenge you. If you have power, value the people who find a way to show you your own conduct.
